title: explainer_kit: exact 8-bit colour via the P010 wire (ffmpeg writes the 8-bit stream)
description:
Found by spike S-5 (commit ae23be9). franken_manim's 8-bit NV12 wire is about 1.5 Cb codes short on dark blue. The corpus background #0E1116 is written as Y 30, Cb 129, Cr 126, where exact BT.709 limited-range codes are 30.37 / 130.50 / 126.48. The result is a slightly green-black background (#0D1112 on screen instead of #0E1116), visible under a contrast stretch and present in every 8-bit deliverable so far, v5's master included.

How it was measured:
- a CRF-0 (lossless) fmn render of a flat background, decoded to raw yuv420p;
- fmn's RGBA8 PNG frames are exact (14, 17, 22);
- fmn's P010 path writes 121 / 522 / 507, which is 130.5 x 4 for Cb, exact;
- ffmpeg's own RGB-to-yuv420p conversion writes 29 / 130 / 126.

The bias is introduced in fmn's fused NV12 conversion. fmn-frame's rgba_to_nv12 on the same pixels would round correctly.

Fix on the corpus side, without touching franken_manim: render on the P010 wire and let ffmpeg write the 8-bit H.264 stream. The kit's QualityRunner already rewrites the encode argv. It can replace fmn's `-pix_fmt yuv420p10le` (P010 in, 10-bit out) with `-pix_fmt yuv420p`, so swscale converts 10 to 8 bits with its rounding and dither, which also helps against banding. Set `file_writer.pixel_format = "p010le"` in delivery renders, including the CLI's options() after delivery_options.

Acceptance:
- A CRF-0 render of a flat #0E1116 frame decodes to Cb within 0.5 of 130.5 and Y within 0.5 of 30.37, against today's 129.
- The same check runs on a palette colour (Hoeffding yellow #FFD866).
- The 4K fps cost of the 2x pipe payload is measured (P010 is 25 MB per frame against NV12's 12 MB) and noted.
- The output stays 8-bit High profile H.264 with BT.709 tags; verify_video.sh passes.
- An integration test in the kit asserts the codes, with ffmpeg on PATH as the CLI tests already require.

Upstream: the same evidence goes into the franken_manim issue packet (U-18; filing needs the owner's OK).

The cause was not fmn's NV12 conversion. fmn's encode argv declares no colour space or range on its raw input (only on the output), so ffmpeg converts the frames from its default matrix. Exact NV12 bytes (30, 130, 126) fed through fmn's argv shape reproduce Cb 129, and come through exact once the input is tagged. The kit's runner now inserts -colorspace bt709 -color_range <output's> before -i - on raw-video jobs, and the NV12 wire stays (no 2x pipe payload, no P010). comments.text: Candidate U-18 (evidence for the owner, not filed): fmn's 8-bit NV12 wire biases chroma. Repro at e2eec632: render a flat #0E1116 background with x264 CRF 0 (lossless), decode to yuv420p: Y 30, Cb 129, Cr 126; exact BT.709 limited codes are 30.37/130.50/126.48 (Cb 1.5 codes low: blue lost, background reads green-black). fmn's RGBA8 frames are exact (PNG 14,17,22), fmn-frame::rgba_to_nv12's quant8 rounds correctly (it would write 130), and the P010 path writes 121/522/507 (exact); so the bias is in the renderer's fused NV12 conversion. comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Correction to candidate U-18 (3851db4): the cause is in fmn-output/src/negotiate.rs encode_argv, which tags the output (-colorspace bt709 -color_range tv) but not the rawvideo input, so ffmpeg converts from its default matrix. The NV12 conversion itself is exact: NV12 bytes 30/130/126 through that argv shape decode as Cb 129, and through it with '-colorspace bt709 -color_range tv' before '-i -' they decode exact. Impact at e2eec632, lossless: #0E1116 Cb 130.5 -> 129; #FFD866 Cr 149.7 -> 146, Y 201.6 -> 203. Suggested upstream fix: emit the input's colour description in encode_argv. The corpus works around it in its runner.
